appearance_facts.fact: Chart title reads 'Product Rating Share by Category'. Plot area spans roughly x=270-1850, y=300-1560.
Six blue circular markers at Quality (~x=450), Price (~x=690), Design (~x=930), Support (~x=1170), Delivery (~x=1410), Other (~x=1650).
Design marker is highest on the page (~y=400); Delivery next (~y=610); Other ~y=680; Price ~y=720; Quality ~y=830; Support lowest (~y=920).
Each marker has a small percentage text label directly above it.

printed_facts.fact: Axis labeled 'Category'; tick labels Quality, Price, Design, Support, Delivery, Other.
Quality=36%, Price=38%, Design=34%, Support=45%, Delivery=43%, Other=53%.
Among the six labeled values, Other (53%) is the largest, followed by Support (45%), Delivery (43%), Price (38%), Quality (36%), Design (34%).

public_definitions: Promotion budget rule: Select the category with the highest current labeled rating share.
Decision metric: mislabeled_value / labeled rating share.
chart_reference: Use the dashboard labeled rating-share values as the evidence source; the promotion budget is reserved for the category with the strongest current rating-share signal.
uncertain: The y-axis 'Value' positions do not match the percentage labels (e.g., Design is plotted highest at ~54 but labeled 34%; Other is plotted ~41 but labeled 53%), so the plotted geometry and the printed labels disagree.
The task's selectable options are only Other, Design, and Support; the highest labeled value (Other, 53%) is among the options, but the visual peak (Design) is not the labeled maximum.
